python_port.verified_against: data/unfold-graph.gml -> 48 vertices, 120 edges, 72 semantic, 48 phase, degree 5
python_port.note: portable reference; the C++ owner stays authoritative for native builds and for FieldDag

why: data/unfold-graph.gml introduces G_runtime = Q3 □ C6 (48 vertices, 120 edges, degree 5). It also exposes two contradictions with the phase grammar that must be resolved in a contract rather than in a comment: (1) phases.ebnf declares Xul terminal and the ladder linear Pop→…→Xul, while the graph closes the cycle with Xul→Pop; (2) the graph spells the fifth phase `Chen` where the grammars spell it `Ch'en`. A third point is not a contradiction but a boundary: the GML supplies topology, not executable permission.

semantic_step.invariant: Hamming distance exactly 1 on the address, phase unchanged

phase_step.invariant: address unchanged, |Δθ| = 1 on the C6 wheel
phase_step.note: 0.5 is cos(π/3), the arc_weight of an adjacent C6 step — the connection's holonomy, not a routing preference

terminal_scope.contradiction: phases.ebnf: Xul is terminal and the pipeline is linear. unfold-graph.gml: Xul → Pop closes the cycle.
terminal_scope.resolution: terminality is scoped to ONE EXECUTION, not to the graph
terminal_scope.law: within an execution the ladder is Pop → Wo → Yax → Sek → Ch'en → Xul and admits no wrap; the Xul → Pop edge exists only as a cycle boundary that starts a NEW execution

consequences.terminal_flag_meaning: no further phase step inside this execution

phase_identity.contradiction: the GML writes `Chen`, the grammars write `Ch'en`
phase_identity.resolution: one identity, canonicalised at the parser boundary
phase_identity.law: the parser canonicalises the token once (world::canonical_phase_name) so no consumer can create a second phase identity
phase_identity.unknown_token_rule: returned unchanged and refused by the runtime graph as unknown_phase — a typo never becomes a phase

authority.admission_owner: XCFE (host callback; topology can never substitute for it)

moves.semantic_step: change the Micronaut address, preserve the phase
moves.phase_step: change the phase forward by one, preserve the address
moves.composite: a sequence of legal atomic moves, each admitted separately

trace.law: a recorded phase step is a candidate route, never an authorization (RG6); the trace records the walk, it does not perform it

fields.phases: one {phase, status, detail} per canonical phase in the order Pop, Wo, Yax, Sek, Ch'en, Xul
fields.steps: ordered {seq, phase, event, detail} log; a redirect starts a child trace with parent set instead of wrapping Xul to Pop inside one record

invariants.RG1: the graph has 48 vertices, 120 edges and degree 5 at every vertex (3 semantic + 2 phase)
invariants.RG2: a semantic edge changes the address by exactly one bit and leaves the phase unchanged
invariants.RG3: a phase edge leaves the address unchanged and moves exactly one C6 step
invariants.RG4: every vertex declares an address in 0..7 and a canonical C6 phase; an unknown phase token is a typed refusal
invariants.RG5: within one execution the phase ladder is forward only (Pop→…→Xul); the Xul→Pop edge is a new-execution boundary and a same-execution wrap is refused
invariants.RG6: a move is only performed when the host admission callback admits it; a legal edge is a candidate route, never an authorization
invariants.RG7: no move mutates the graph: the topology, its vertex count and its edge count are identical before and after
